criterion: every changed path matches a ## Scope glob; a recorded two-way-door entry covers the deviation
finding: Out-of-scope path: decision D-5 cannot sanction it, because a Scope change is outside agent authority
why: The protocol makes a fork a two-way door only when it reshapes no Scope glob, and D-5 itself states that it adds a path outside Scope, so the fork had to park for the owner; this file is also the install manifest that every v1 Codex user reads, and D-5 marks the Codex behavior as not verified.
fix: Get an owner ruling and add the path to the 0001 ## Scope, or remove the entry and its test and park the Codex install path for the owner.
evidence: DECISIONS.md (plugin root): "Inside agent authority. ... it reshapes no plan structure (Scope globs, subtask graph, declared Produces/Consumes seams)" and "One-way door, or a tie — any condition fails → the caller's park/ask path". plan-s1/DECISIONS.md:35: "Supersedes: none (0001 ## Scope lists only .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; this adds one path outside it)". PROVIDERS.md: "codex plugin marketplace add reads the Codex marketplace manifest from that path".

criterion: Test weakened to pass
finding: The 50 ms test now passes on the best of up to five medians, and D-7 wrongly says a slower hook fails all five attempts
why: The change widens the tolerance of the AC-013 gate to stop a timing failure, so the test passes the head hook in runs where most medians are over the limit, and DECISIONS.md:48 states a guarantee that the rule does not give.
fix: Judge one number over all attempts (for example the median of the medians), or keep the retry and correct D-7 to say the gate is the lowest median of five, with the owner told of the weaker gate.
evidence: test_hooks.py:118 `if medians[-1] < 0.050:` then `return`; DECISIONS.md:48 "A hook that is slower than 50 ms fails all five attempts". Separate probe at head on session-start.cmd, 20 medians of 7, other reviewers running on the machine: median of medians 51.6 ms, 11 of 20 at 50 ms or more, and all 4 groups of five pass under the retry rule. Not measured: a hook slowed by a controlled small amount.

criterion: open question: most important problem that no checklist item covers
finding: Second gate bypass: no plan step or decision owns how the v2 files pass the v1 gates, and the v1 test job is red on them
why: The in-scope file afkv2/tests/live/CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md trips the native-contract gate, which also feeds the v1 gate tests in scripts/tests, and the rule 'at ship, CI must be green' has no owner because a search of docs/afk/afkv2 for native-contract and plugin-source finds only these journal lines; the base branch already holds 147 same-rule lines per the journal, so this change adds to the cause and is not the sole cause.
fix: Record who resolves it: name a plan step or an owner decision for a native-contract treatment of afkv2/ and docs/afk/afkv2, and stop treating it as journal-only friction.
evidence: JOURNAL.md:18: "the v1 plugin gate refused the review-fix commit ... committed with AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES=1". PR 155 at d2239c37, job 123911122760, step 'Unit tests' failure: "20 failed, 3710 passed"; failure text: "afkv2/tests/live/CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md:11: forbidden harness-name vocabulary". Step 'Plugin-source gates' skipped, and .github/workflows/tests.yml:99 runs it with no override: "bash hooks/plugin-source-gates.sh --range "$base" HEAD || { echo "::error::plugin-source gates blocked"; exit 1; }".

criterion: open-question
finding: The new bracket block makes a `)` in %DATE% or %TIME% a parse error, so the hook exits 255 and writes no record (subagent-start.cmd:11 has the same line)
why: This fix was meant to stop the record from failing the hook, but it adds a new way to fail that the previous revision did not have; logic-correctness owns this class, and it is here in the one open-question slot because a probe proved it.
fix: Do not expand %DATE% or %TIME% inside the block: echo only the provider and event and let the file time carry the time (not verified: that S3 setup reads only the file time), and add a test with a DATE value that holds a bracket.
evidence: Probe with env DATE="Thu (10/30/2026)": head gives rc 255, stderr b'1:46:34.00) was unexpected at this time.\r\n', and the text is already printed; the same DATE on efd83cdb session-start.cmd gives rc 0, stderr b'', record b'claude session-start Thu (10/30/2026)  1:50:09.11\r\n'. Inferred, not probed: a custom Windows short-date format with a bracket reaches %DATE% the same way; a harness may drop stdout on a non-zero exit (not verified).

criterion: Documented-rule breach in changed lines
finding: The bare-word check runs only on CODE_SUFFIXES, so a v1 name in a CSS class, a storage key or a .tsx/.jsx/.vue file passes, and D-6 records a smaller gap than the real one
why: 0001 Acceptance requires a failure on the v1 name in storage keys and CSS classes, D-6 says every file flags a CSS class and names only a prose sentence as the known gap, but the file-type split exempts all HTML, CSS, JSON and YAML to allow one manifest description.
fix: Add the missing script suffixes to CODE_SUFFIXES, flag a `-name` suffix inside a CSS selector, class attribute and quoted JSON value, and write the remaining gap into D-6.
evidence: Probe through check_no_v1_names on a scratch tree, flagged=False: sample.css `.card-afk { color: red }`; sample.html `<div class="card-afk">`; sample.json `{"key": "draft-afk"}`; sample.yaml `env: MY_AFK`; sample.tsx `const afk = 1`; sample.jsx `run(afk)`; sample.vue `const afk = 1`. flagged=True on sample.py `k = "draft-afk"`. Line 86: `patterns = (*V1_TEXT, V1_WORD_IN_CODE) if path.suffix.lower() in CODE_SUFFIXES else V1_TEXT`.

criterion: 0001 Acceptance: fail on a v1 name in CSS classes and storage keys
finding: The no-v1-name rule passes a CSS class or a storage key that ends in '-af' + 'k' in HTML and CSS files, and every bare word in .html, .css, .tsx and .jsx files.
why: The class pattern excludes a '-' before the name, and CODE_SUFFIXES has no .html, .css, .tsx or .jsx, so the forms that the SDD no-v1-name row names escape the check in the files that hold them.
fix: Remove '-' from the class pattern look-behind, add a pattern for a quoted key or a CSS selector that ends in the name, and add .html, .css, .jsx and .tsx to the suffix set that gets V1_WORD_IN_CODE (the D-6 code-file rule).
evidence: Probe of check_no_v1_names, False = not flagged (v1 word written as af+k): sample.html '<div class="my-afk">' False; sample.css '.my-afk { color: red }' False; sample.css '#afk { color: red }' False; sample.html "<script>localStorage.getItem('draft-afk')</script>" False; sample.html '<script>const afk = 1;</script>' False; sample.html '<div class=afk>' False; sample.tsx 'const afk = 1;' False; sample.jsx 'const afk = 1;' False.

criterion: 0001 Acceptance: the v1-name check must not fail open on input it cannot read
finding: A code file that is not UTF-8 is skipped in silence, so the v1-name check and the marker check pass it with a v1 variable in it.
why: _text_lines returns no lines on UnicodeDecodeError, and a Windows .cmd or .ps1 file in a legacy code page or UTF-16 is a normal input on the one supported platform for these hooks, so the check reports a clean tree that it did not read.
fix: Report a problem for a file with a code suffix that does not decode as UTF-8, or decode it with a fallback; skip only binary files.
evidence: Probe: sample.cmd with bytes of 'set AFK_X=1\r\nrem caf\xe9\r\n' (latin-1) -> check_no_v1_names lines for sample.cmd: []; the same line written as UTF-16 -> []. The same line in UTF-8 is flagged by the existing test line 'echo %AFK_X%' form.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros); D-5 'the v1 entry stays as is' and '"installation": "AVAILABLE" installs nothing until the owner enables it'; AGENTS.md opt-in boundary
finding: The Codex marketplace test pins only source, so a default-on afkv2 policy and a changed v1 entry both pass
why: D-5 rests on a pure addition with an AVAILABLE policy, and the sibling Claude test pins the whole v1 entry, but this test checks neither fact.
fix: Assert the whole entry dict for both names, including policy and category.
evidence: Line: 'assert entries[V1]["source"] == {"source": "local", "path": "./"}'. Scratch mutants of .agents/plugins/marketplace.json: 'SURVIVED codex afkv2 policy default-on :: 86 passed, 1 xfailed' and 'SURVIVED codex v1 entry category changed :: 86 passed, 1 xfailed'.

criterion: Open question: the most important problem no checklist item covers
finding: No CI job runs afkv2/tests, so none of these tests guards a later change
why: The tests workflow runs only scripts/tests and the hook smoke script, the user rule keeps the full suite off local runs, and no plan-s* step, SDD row or PRD row adds this tree to CI.

Pattern 'afkv2/tests|afkv2.tests' over scripts/tests: no hit. Pattern 'tests.yml|.github|continuous integration|in CI|CI job' over docs/afk/afkv2/plan-s*/*.md, SDD.md, PRD.md: one hit, PRD.md:209, about manual CI jobs only.

finding: The committed journal line points to a session scratch file for the gate output instead of holding the facts
why: The scratch folder is specific to one session on one machine, so a later reader cannot open it, and JOURNAL-FORMAT.md says the journal lets a human who was not watching reconstruct what happened from the journal alone.

criterion: 0001 Acceptance: fail on a v1 name in environment variables and storage keys
finding: A name that ends in '_' + the v1 word passes in code files, because V1_WORD_IN_CODE treats '_' as a word character and no other pattern covers that form.
why: The SDD row says the v1 word not followed by v2 fails over environment variables and storage keys, and these forms are one of each.
fix: Remove '_' from the V1_WORD_IN_CODE look-behind, and add one test for each form.
evidence: Probe of check_no_v1_names, False = not flagged: sample.cmd 'set MY_AFK=1' False; sample.py "os.environ['MY_AFK']" False; sample.py "localStorage.getItem('draft_afk')" False.

criterion: D-6: a bare word in a text file passes as prose
finding: A prose sentence in a text file that has the v1 word before a full stop or a colon fails the check, against the rule of D-6.
why: The look-ahead accepts '.' and ':' at the end of the word without a following name character, so normal punctuation counts as a name form, and test_prose_passes_outside_code does not try this input.
fix: Require a name character after the separator, for example (?=[-_:./\\][a-z0-9]|[a-z0-9]), and add the two sentences to the prose test.
evidence: Probe of check_no_v1_names, True = flagged: sample.md 'Compare with AFK. Then go on.' True; sample.md 'Run AFK: then stop.' True. D-6: 'a bare word in other text files passes as prose'.

criterion: 0001 Acceptance: fail on code that matches a marker by a prefix or substring
finding: Same-line substring and prefix marker matches in languages that the check scans pass, because the operator list has no JS '.test(', PowerShell 'Select-String', 'sed' or slice compare.
why: D-4 records only data flow through a variable as a known gap, and these forms hold the marker and the operator on one line in suffixes that CODE_SUFFIXES lists.
fix: Add '.test(', 'Select-String', 'sls' and 'sed' to SUBSTRING_MATCH, and flag a slice compare beside a marker token; add each form to test_prefix_or_substring_marker_match_fails.
evidence: Probe of check_marker_matching, False = not flagged: s.js '/afkv2-core-behaviors/.test(line)' False; s.ps1 'Select-String -Pattern "afkv2-core-behaviors" x.txt' False; s.sh 'sed -n "/afkv2-core-behaviors/p" x' False; s.py 'line[:20] == "afkv2-core-behaviors"' False; s.js 'line.slice(0,5) === "afkv2-core-behaviors"' False.

criterion: empty/null inputs: a registration check must see a registration
finding: The check answers ok when a hook event has an empty or null registration, so the hook never fires and the tree still passes.
why: The delta guards the 'hooks' value but the event loop tests only that the key exists, so the same null input one level down still passes.
fix: Report 'no {event} registration' when events.get(event) is not a non-empty list.
evidence: Probe: hooks.json '{"hooks": {"SessionStart": [], "SubagentStart": null}}' -> plugin_check.py exit 0, stdout '{"ok": true, "verb": "check", ...'.

criterion: error paths: the command answers one JSON object
finding: An unreadable source or prebuilt file makes the command print a traceback and no JSON, although the module docstring says it answers one JSON object.
why: The delta makes usage errors JSON, but run_checks and build still raise on UnicodeDecodeError and OSError, so a caller that parses stdout gets an empty string; the exit code is still 1, so the check does not pass.
fix: Catch OSError and UnicodeDecodeError in _read_source, _check_built and the build write, and report each as a problem; a prebuilt file that does not decode is stale.
evidence: Probe: CORE-BEHAVIORS.md = b'\xff\xfe bad\n' -> check and build: rc=1, stdout '', stderr ends "UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0". Prebuilt .txt = b'\xff bad' -> check: rc=1, stdout '', the same error. Prebuilt .txt is a folder -> build: rc=1, stdout '', traceback ending in the path of that folder.

criterion: Fragile test: asserts coupled to shared state; own the fixture (Meszaros)
finding: The no-data-folder test probes the real drive root and does not assert stderr
why: A folder that exists before the run gives a false red, a broken guard writes outside the test folder and leaves every later run red, and a hook that fails to create the folder at the root passes (inferred from reading; the guard-removed mutant was not run, to keep the drive root clean).
fix: Assert stderr is empty as the sibling test does, and fail with a clear message when the folder exists before the run.
evidence: Line: 'assert not (Path(tmp_path.anchor) / "afkv2").exists()'. The test has no 'done.stderr' assert; test_data_folder_path_with_brackets_gets_the_record has one. Probe of the hook's set line with LOCALAPPDATA undefined: 'resolved=C:\afkv2'.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): negative case missing beside a new guard
finding: The new hooks-value test covers the wrong-type guard, but no test covers the missing-event branch directly below it
why: The plugin check can lose its 'no {event} registration' rule and the suite stays green; only the shipped hooks.json is pinned, by Windows-only tests of the file and not of the check.
fix: Add a case per event in HOOK_EVENTS that deletes the event from hooks.json and asserts the 'no <event> registration' problem.
evidence: Scratch mutant of afkv2/scripts/plugin_check.py:165 'if event not in events:' to 'if False:': 'SURVIVED no event registration loop :: 86 passed, 1 xfailed'.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): 0001 Acceptance lists environment variables and CSS classes
finding: Four name forms that the new patterns accept have no test case: a forward-slash path part, ${name}, className=, and name\path with no separator before it
why: In a text file only these pattern parts catch those forms, so narrowing a pattern removes the rule for that form with no red test.
fix: Add the four lines to the parameter list; test_v1_name_in_text_fails already runs each one against sample.txt.
evidence: Scratch mutants of V1_TEXT: 'SURVIVED path-part without slash', 'SURVIVED dollar without brace', 'SURVIVED class regex no className', 'SURVIVED no backslash in follow set', each '86 passed, 1 xfailed'.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): D-6 'code files also flag the bare word'
finding: The bare-word test runs only on .py, although the plugin's hooks are .cmd and CODE_SUFFIXES lists nine suffixes
why: The rule can shrink to Python files and the suite stays green, so a bare v1 word in a hook is not proven to fail.
fix: Parametrize the file name over every suffix in plugin_check.CODE_SUFFIXES.
evidence: Line: '(tree / "scripts" / "sample.py").write_text(line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")'. Scratch mutant of 'if path.suffix.lower() in CODE_SUFFIXES else V1_TEXT' to '== ".py"': 'SURVIVED word-in-code only .py :: 86 passed, 1 xfailed'.

criterion: Assertion strength: 0001 Acceptance answer shape '{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "reason"}}' (config reader); same shape in plugin_check.py
finding: The usage-error tests do not assert ok is false, so a usage answer with ok true passes
why: A caller reads ok first, and the same gap is in afkv2/tests/test_config.py:171 (by reading; that mutant was not run).
